[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Apache Spark: Aggregations and Grouping Strategies"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Data aggregation is a core workload in big data processing. Apache Spark provides robust mechanisms to group data and compute summary statistics. This tutorial explores fundamental aggregation techniques and advanced grouping strategies using the Spark DataFrame API."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Basic Grouping and Aggregations"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The groupBy method is the primary entry point for grouping data. Once a DataFrame is grouped, you can apply aggregate functions like sum, avg, max, min, and count."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import avg, sum, max, col

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("AggregationTutorial").getOrCreate()

# Sample DataFrame creation
data = [("IT", 3000), ("IT", 4000), ("HR", 2500), ("HR", 3000), ("Finance", 5000)]
df = spark.createDataFrame(data, ["Department", "Salary"])

# Basic grouping by department and calculating average salary
result_df = df.groupBy("Department").agg(
    avg("Salary").alias("Average_Salary"),
    sum("Salary").alias("Total_Salary")
)

result_df.show()"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Advanced Grouping Strategies"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"For more complex OLAP workloads, Spark offers advanced grouping functions such as rollup and cube. These methods allow you to calculate subtotals and grand totals efficiently."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"rollup(): Creates hierarchical subtotals going from right to left in the specified columns, ending with a grand total."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"cube(): Creates all possible combinations of subtotals for the specified grouping columns, plus a grand total."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"# Using rollup for hierarchical aggregations
sales_data = [("North", "Laptop", 1000), ("North", "Phone", 500), ("South", "Laptop", 1200)]
sales_df = spark.createDataFrame(sales_data, ["Region", "Product", "Sales"])

rollup_df = sales_df.groupBy("Region", "Product").rollup("Region", "Product").sum("Sales")
rollup_df.show()"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Window Functions for Complex Analytics"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Sometimes you need to compute aggregations without collapsing your DataFrame into fewer rows. Window functions allow you to perform sliding or partitioning calculations across rows."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql.functions import rank

windowSpec = Window.partitionBy("Department").orderBy(col("Salary").desc())
ranked_df = df.withColumn("rank", rank().over(windowSpec))
ranked_df.show()"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Spark Aggregations"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Minimize data shuffling by filtering your DataFrame early before applying groupBy operations."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Be cautious with high-cardinality columns in groupBy, as they can cause severe network shuffle bottlenecks and out-of-memory errors."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use built-in Spark SQL functions instead of UDFs (User Defined Functions) whenever possible for optimized execution plans."}]
